chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His saying, 'Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good,' [the first 'good' refers to] the pleasure of Allah and Paradise in the Hereafter, and [the second 'good' refers to] livelihood and good character in this world.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'good in this world and good in the Hereafter' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a nuanced exegesis of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:201, distinguishing between the dual aspects of 'goodness' (hasanah). While the summary provided in the prompt contains a common interpretive variation, this specific chain emphasizes that the 'goodness in this world' refers to sustenance (ma'ash) and noble character (husn al-khuluq), whereas the 'goodness in the Hereafter' is identified as divine pleasure (ridwan) and Paradise. This interpretation highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual devotion with ethical conduct and material well-being in daily life.
